bri.invariant module¶

Backbone Rigid Invariant (BRI) computation module.

This module provides functions for computing and analyzing backbone rigid invariants of protein structures. It includes functionality for:

  • Extending invariants with bond and torsion angles

  • Generating invariant summaries

  • Computing coordinate transformations and basis vectors

The module implements the mathematical foundations of the BRI method as described in the associated research papers.

bri.invariant.get_invariant_BTP(invariant: DataFrame) → DataFrame¶

Computes bond-torsion-point (BTP) invariant (from BRI).

Bond-torsion-point (BTP) invariant is a complete invariant simpler than both BRI and AL. It consists of three 2-bond lengths (diagonal length skipping one intermediate atom) \(C_{i-1}A_i, N_iC_i, A_iN_{i+1}\), and three torsion points TP(bond) = (bond_length*cos(torsion_angle), bond_length*sin(torsion_angle)) for 3 bonds \(C_{i-1}N_i, N_iA_i, A_iC_i\) and corresponding torsion angles at these bonds.

This BTP invariant saves 9 mentioned values per residue as: |C-N-A|, |N-A-C|, |A-C-N|, TP(CN)_x, TP(CN)_y, TP(NA)_x, TP(NA)_y, TP(AC)_x, TP(AC)_y.

Parameters:

invariant – BRI of a chain with angles

Returns:

bond-torsion-point (BTP) invariant

bri.invariant.invariant_ext(invariant: DataFrame) → DataFrame¶

Extend an input invariant by computing bond and torsion angles from it.

Parameters:

invariant – A backbone-rigid-invariant with complete 3 weaker invariants and 9 stronger invariants at least.

Returns:

Extended backbone-rigid-invariant with bond and torsion angles.

bri.invariant.get_invariant_summary(invariant: DataFrame, bond_length: bool = True, min_and_max: bool = False) → DataFrame¶

Compute backbone-rigid-invariant summary consisting of averages and standard deviations.

Parameters:

  • invariant – Backbone-Rigid-Invariant of a chain

  • bond_length – If input BRI includes bond length. Default True.

  • min_and_max – If to compute minimum and maximum of input BRI. Default False.

Returns:

Summary of input invariant.

bri.invariant.get_invariant(chain: DataFrame, ext: bool = False) → DataFrame¶

Computes backbone-rigid-invariant

Parameters:

  • chain – A pandas.DataFrame that represents a chain with atomic coordinates.

  • ext – Include bond angles and torsion angles. Default False.

Returns:

3-decimal alpha-invariant of a chain

bri.invariant.row_trans(row: Series, last_row: Series | None = None, update_atoms: List[str] = ['N', 'CA', 'C'], o: str = 'CA', orthogonal: bool = True) → Series¶

Transform coordinates to a new basis.

Parameters:

  • row – Current row of coordinates

  • last_row – Previous row of coordinates (optional)

  • update_atoms – List of atoms to update, defaults to [“N”, “CA”, “C”]

  • o – Origin atom, defaults to “CA”

  • orthogonal – Whether to use orthogonal basis, defaults to True

Returns:

Transformed coordinates

bri.invariant.get_basis(row: Series, o: str = 'CA', v1_p: str = 'N', v2_p: str = 'C', orthogonal: bool = False) → List[ndarray]¶

Get basis vectors for coordinate transformation.

Parameters:

  • row – Row of coordinates

  • o – Origin atom, defaults to “CA”

  • v1_p – First vector point, defaults to “N”

  • v2_p – Second vector point, defaults to “C”

  • orthogonal – Whether to use orthogonal basis, defaults to True

Returns:

List of 3 basis vectors
